SYMNAV #127
QUESTION 02 OF 07

From the overview ↗   Five caches store promises by symbol identity; one stores locations by position. Public projections can be rebuilt.

If lifetime is shared, why keep six caches?

They share a reset boundary. They do not share a namespace. Each handle still has its own Map and its own value type.

ISOLATED HANDLE	KEY STAYS	STORED VALUE STAYS
definitionsByIdentity	formatted symbol identity	promise of symbol overview nodes
referencesByIdentity	formatted symbol identity	promise of semantic reference locations
callTargetsByIdentity	formatted symbol identity	promise of call-target resolution
callersByIdentity	formatted symbol identity	promise of incoming call edges
calleesByIdentity	formatted symbol identity	promise of outgoing call edges
definitionsByPosition	relative path + ":" + start offset	array of semantic node locations
ONE DISCOVERY, TWO PROJECTIONS
referenceLocations(identity)
cached promise
path · start · length · isDefinition
↠
findCallers
CallerFinder → separately cached caller promise
findReferences
rebuilds public reference objects on each call

“Exact promise identity” refers to the cache entry and the service methods that return it directly. It does not describe every backend wrapper or the public reference projection.

POSITION RESULTS REMEMBER LOCATIONS, THEN REHYDRATE NODES
identifier position
→
cached locations [path, start, kind]
→
node lookup on every access

Two returned node arrays can be different arrays containing the same node. Empty location arrays are cached too.

D3 · stated
One scope, six independent handles.

The PR chooses isolation because the existing queries have independent key and value spaces. The same string can be present in two handles without joining their answers.

The six declarations and PR decision →
D4 · stated
Store the exact value; check presence with Map.has.

The PR explicitly preserves identities and treats undefined as a valid cached value. No copying, promise wrapping, or truthiness test occurs inside getOrCreate.
